My conclusion is that SS Solar, Verdant Solar and Solana Tec are particularly worth considering for residential solar, while Ditrolic Energy stands out for larger commercial or industrial installations.

I would not choose solely by a five-star Google rating. For a solar installation expected to operate for 20–30 years, the company's technical competence, workmanship, financial stability and after-sales service matter just as much.

What the reviews tell us

There are some important differences behind the ratings.

SS Solar: Its website publishes customer feedback praising neat wiring, clear explanations and after-sales support. Its parent engineering company, Swee Seng Electrical Engineering, appears in SEDA's provider directory. However, the 1985 history belongs to the electrical business, not necessarily decades of solar installation experience. 
SS Solar
+1

Solana Tec: Several detailed reviews mention specific engineers, project coordination, reasonable pricing and post-installation responsiveness. These are encouraging signs beyond generic five-star reviews. 
findcontractor.my

Verdant Solar: Its broader company review profile shows 4.7/5 from 766 reviews. There are positive reports of prompt inverter replacement and good monitoring support, but also a detailed complaint about installation timing, Wi-Fi setup and rebate documentation. I would investigate those issues before signing. 
4.7/5 from 766 Customer Reviews

How I would check whether a company is trustworthy

Before paying a deposit, I would require:

SEDA registration: Verify the exact contracting company at the official SEDA directory. Registration is a qualification check, not a government endorsement.

Local references: Contact two customers whose installations are at least 12 months old, ideally in Johor Bahru.

Written warranties: Separate warranties for solar panels, inverter, installation workmanship and roof leakage.

After-sales commitment: Written response times for inverter failure, water leakage and system underperformance.

Transparent quotation: Exact panel and inverter models, system capacity, expected annual generation, realistic payback calculations and payment milestones.

My recommendation

For a residential installation in 81100, I would contact SS Solar first, Solana Tec second and Verdant Solar third. I would compare their quotations before deciding. SS Solar's local engineering background is promising, while Solana Tec has particularly substantial and detailed positive customer feedback.

For a factory or major commercial installation, I would include Ditrolic Energy.

Useful direct websites: SS Solar, Solana Tec, Verdant Solar.

Eternalgy's strongest competitive advantages

Eternalgy stands out in three areas: its reported CIDB G7 contractor grade, its independently listed SEDA PV Investor status for leasing/PPA arrangements, and its MyHIJAU-certified EPCC service. Its published warranty package and monitoring arrangements are additional positives. 
Eternalgy
+3

Its biggest competitive challenge is not necessarily technical capability. It is demonstrating its capabilities through independently verifiable project references and a larger history of customer feedback. Its reported 12 MWp and 1,100+ installations are encouraging, but project counts alone do not establish installation quality, long-term system yield or after-sales reliability.

My conclusion

For a residential solar customer, I would shortlist Solana Tec, Verdant Solar and Amiya Energy alongside Eternalgy.

For a commercial or industrial project, I would take Eternalgy especially seriously because of its reported G7 status, investor registration and financing options, while comparing its engineering proposal against Solana Tec and SS Solar.

Eternalgy at 8.4/10 is a strong contender, not an industry laggard. Its credentials may justify an even higher technical-capability score, but I would want independently confirmed project performance and customer references before moving it above 9/10.

The scores are indicative assessments, not the result of site inspections, audited financials or verified installation-performance data. I would not treat differences of 0.1–0.3 points as conclusive.

One important detail: warranties

Solana Tec publishes a two-year workmanship warranty covering mounting, roof penetrations and installation-related electrical work. It also advertises lifetime customer support, but that is not the same as a lifetime warranty.

Eternalgy advertises three years of workmanship coverage, giving it an advantage on the stated warranty duration.

Before signing with either company, I would require:

Exact panel and inverter models, with manufacturer warranty documents.

Written workmanship and roof-leak coverage.

Two recent Johor customer references for comparable installations.

A detailed savings projection based on your actual TNB bills and the current Solar ATAP rules.

A written after-sales response commitment.

Final verdict

My pick remains Solana Tec Sdn Bhd - Solar Panel Energy Johor, primarily because of its stronger customer review history, longer operating record, and documented Johor projects. It is the company I would contact first.
